description:
Found on develop at d91cae495 ("Corrected call signature for dbg"), which
declares `extern "fz" defp fz_dbg_value(t) :: t when t: any`. That declaration
is correct; it exposed a leak `fz_send` and `fz_make_resource` already had.
Prior art: commit 4c4595502 (on the
unmerged fz-kdt.98.3.17.10/restart branch), not adopted here -- see
"Not adopted").

## Reds this closes (develop @ d91cae495)

- `compiler2::fixture_contract_harness_test::compiler2_contracts` -- 00548..00552
  `.call_edges`: every `Kernel.dbg/1(T) => T => T` line reads `=> a0 => a0`.
  The committed snapshots are the paper answer; they are NOT re-blessed.
- `compiler2::drive_test::compiler2_tuple_return_ladder_revises_once_per_nesting_level`
  -- `TUPLE_LADDER_MAIN_RETURN_REVISIONS` measures 1, pinned 2: main/0 settles
  once, on the leaked `a0`. Re-measure after the fix and state the value it
  lands on with its cause (a lowering is authorized by the owner).

## Reduced cases and paper answers

`target/debug/fz2 run --dump activations=OUT.acts FILE.fz`

| program | measured | paper |
|---|---|---|
| `def main(), do: dbg(1)` | main/0 `a0`, `dbg/1(int) => a0` | `int` |
| `def main(), do: send(self(), 1)` | main/0 `a1` | `int` |
| `def drop(_x), do: nil` / `make_resource(1, &drop/1)` | `resource(a0)` | `resource(int)` |
| `@spec id(t) :: t when t: any; def id(x), do: x; id(1)` | `int` | `int` (control) |

Order case, ported as a test (not as mechanism) from 4c4595502's
`fixtures2/behavior/extern_return_binds_to_caller.fz`: `ascending/0` =
`dbg(11); dbg(10.5)` => `float`; `descending/0` = `dbg(10.5); dbg(11)` => `int`.
Its header must describe contract-owned instantiation, not "unifying".

## Mechanism (measured by two readers, telemetry + code)

Three answers to "what does this activation return", and the wrong one wins:

1. `jobs/semantic.rs:216` -- `LoweredBody::Extern` seeds `return_evidence` with
   `LoweredExtern.return_ty`, the declared result un-instantiated (`a0`),
   posing as an observation.
2. `jobs/semantic.rs:261-267` -- `activation_contract_return` ->
   `FunctionContract::apply` -> `match_arrow` computes the right `int`, at every
   hop (fz_dbg_value, dbg, main), but only as a refinement of (1).
3. `jobs/semantic.rs:1805-1829` `refine_observed_return` -- reads a var-carrying
   observed as "unconstrained", then `intersect(a0, int)` is empty (a bare var
   is a disjoint `vars`-axis literal, types/descr.rs:135) so it falls back to
   observed `a0`. Each caller re-derives `int` and loses it the same way; same
   for `resource(a0)` via `ResourceSig::intersect_pos`.

Behind the seed is a duplicate authority: an extern's declaration is resolved
twice with the same resolver -- `jobs/contract.rs:99` (the `FunctionContract`
fact) and `jobs/body.rs:1592-1643` `resolve_extern_signature` (the parallel
`LoweredExtern.semantic_contract` / `return_ty`).

## The fold: an extern's body is its contract

- An extern activation's return evidence is its own `FunctionContract` applied
  to the activation's row -- the one call-instantiation calculator
  (`match_arrow`, polarity-aware, bounds closed). Set directly, not via
  `refine_call_return`: the declaration is the only witness an extern has.
- When the contract cannot answer (`Underconstrained`, or the row is outside
  the domain) the evidence is not-yet-known (`None`), never `none`; the
  activation waits for grounded inputs.
- `LoweredExtern` carries only the physical ABI (wire params/ret). Its wire
  derivation reads declared types and bounds from the `FunctionContract` fact.

## Removal ledger

| removed | question | survivor |
|---|---|---|
| extern arm seed, semantic.rs:216 | extern activation return | `FunctionContract::apply` on the row |
| `LoweredExtern.return_ty` | same | same |
| `LoweredExtern.semantic_contract` + second `resolve_spec_decl` in body.rs | extern's declared signature | `FunctionContract` fact |

## Not adopted

4c4595502's `collect_instantiation_subst` + `instantiate` in the extern arm: a
non-polarity Unify-mode template matcher (closure literals, aliases, dispatch
templates), i.e. a second calculator for call instantiation. Its
extern-specific return skeleton targets files that do not exist on develop.

## Prediction (r1, cold compile)

`fz_dbg_value[int]`, `dbg[int]`, `main/0` each define their return once, as
`int` -- same event count as today, correct value. Verify with
`--log-telemetry` `return_type defined` events.

## Acceptance

- Reduced cases + order fixture on interp, JIT and AOT, answers as above.
- 00548..00552 match their committed snapshots unchanged.
- Ladder pin re-measured, value and cause stated.
- Full gate: `cargo test --workspace --all-features` + `--doc`, clippy -D warnings.

## Docs in the same commit

- `.agent/docs/externs.md`: the dbg section still shows `fz_dbg_value(any) :: any`;
  "Resource typing" claims `resource(integer)` (false today, true after).
- `.agent/docs/specs.md`: an extern's return is contract application.
- `.agent/docs/semantic-authorities.md`: add a row -- "what does an activation
  return" -- naming its owner.

## Found by the first build (worktree /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-kmu, uncommitted)

The fold as specified turns the two reds green, keeps 00548..00552 unchanged,
keeps the ladder pin at 2, and matches the r1 prediction. The full suite then
shows new reds; two causes are verified and filed as blockers (variadic
contracts; untruthful fz_send declaration). Both surface the same way: a row
that is permanently outside an extern's contract gets no answer, "not yet
known" coincides with `none` at the fixpoint (semantic.rs:208-212), the
continuation is specialized to `compiler2_unreachable_control`, and the native
doors trap (SIGILL). The remaining reds are being classified (pin drop /
honest representation / more specific events / regression) before any is
judged.

A third defect is in the build itself: `resolve_extern_signature` expects the
extern's FunctionContract to carry an arrow, but a refused contract (a wire
spelling inside a tuple, `compiler2_wire_spelling_inside_a_tuple_states_the_rule_it_breaks`)
publishes none; the refusal must reach the compile as the Fatal diagnostic it
was before, not a panic.

## BLOCKED BY

- ○ fz-xxd.1 P1 A variadic extern's contract does not describe its tail
- ○ fz-xxd.2 P1 fz_send declares a narrower domain than Kernel.send forwards
- ○ fz-xxd.5 P1 Contract application answers no row that only overlaps a clause's domain
- ○ fz-xxd.6 P1 An extern row outside its contract is a silent runtime trap, not a compile error

## UNBLOCKS

- ○ fz-xxd.4 P1 refine_observed_return reads a free variable two ways: probe, then delete or reconcile

## Classified reds of the first build (membership diffs, readers C and D)

Behavior regressions, each owned by a blocker of this ticket:
- variadic arity (c_int_negative_return, variadic_three_integers,
  aot_variadic_open, the lib JIT variadic case) -> fz-xxd.1
- fz_send narrower than Kernel.send (concurrency_ping_pong, relay,
  multi_relay, three_process_chain, send_dead_unknown_pid,
  shared_heap_send_large_bitstring, spawn_with_captures,
  receive_selective_refs, two fz2_cli receive tests) -> fz-xxd.2; the scan of
  every lib extern found no other narrower declaration
- truthful declaration, `any` row overlapping the domain (resource_claim,
  file_runtime) -> fz-xxd.5
- silent unreachable trap instead of a diagnostic -> fz-xxd.6

Work pins that rise, all with one shape (base -> new, measured by CLI
capture matching the pins exactly):
| pin | delta | H | R |
|---|---|---|---|
| enum_reduce_operator_refs / drain arbiter (00181) | 399 -> 405 | +2 DeriveFunctionContract | +4 LowerFunction 2->3 |
| work_start_reason census (00420) | 3813 -> 3860 | +18 DeriveFunctionContract | +28 LowerFunction 2->3, +2 AnalyzeActivation, -1 Enum.count/1 |
| range_map semantic formula work | 1048 -> 1081 | +12 DeriveFunctionContract | +21 LowerFunction 2->3 |

H: one DeriveFunctionContract per extern clause already lowered in base; the
declaration resolve used to happen inside LowerFunction (the deleted second
resolve), so this is the same work, recorded. R: an extern's LowerFunction
now starts, blocks on FunctionContract, and retries -- the fz-afu.2 defect
(jobs start before their inputs exist) paying for one more input. After
fz-afu.2 the R part is predicted to vanish; the pins then move by the H part
only, which still needs the owner's authorization as a raise.
title: An extern's return is its contract applied to its row; resolve the declaration once
